metadata.description: A named reference to a credential held by a credential-issuing provider — the target every secrets-as-reference field points at (Compute.Container/Software.Service `credential_ref`, Auth Provider bind refs). It declares WHICH credential (closed type vocabulary), held WHERE (issuer + provider-side secret_path), at what assurance floor — never the value. Resolved at realization by the provider; the value flows directly to the authorized consumer, never through DCM. Secret material NEVER appears in the data model, audit, source control, or logs (docs/spec/governance/credentials.md §1.1).

credential_type.description: Which kind of credential this references — resolves to the matching Credential.* resource the issuer holds (credentials.md §2).

issuer_ref.description: Reference to the issuing provider or CA record — the issuer of this credential. Common-elements Reference shape (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable and policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

secret_path.description: The provider-side path/handle the issuer resolves the value at (e.g. "providers/kubevirt/service-account"). Only the path is ever recorded — never the value.

version.description: Advisory version pin (`latest` or a specific version); the issuer resolves it and records the concrete version in outputs (audit, not the value).

scope.description: What the credential is scoped to (least-privilege) — mirrors the credential_record scope in credentials.md §5; the provider enforces.

entity_uuid.description: Scoped to a specific entity, when applicable.

operations.description: The operations this credential may perform (credentials.md operation vocabulary).

required_assurance.description: The minimum assurance the consumer requires — NIST 800-63B AAL (credentials.md §12.2). A provider whose credential capability cannot reach this floor is filtered out before binding (declare-and-select).

resolved.description: Whether the reference has been bound to a concrete credential at the issuer (Realized). NEVER the value.

resolved_version.description: The concrete credential version the issuer bound (audit record; provider-filled). Not the value.

first_retrieval_at.description: When the credential was first retrieved by the authorized consumer (credentials.md audits first retrieval — AUD hook). Never the value.

relationships.name: authenticates
relationships.description: The workload/service-account identity this credential authenticates, when it is a service-account token or workload credential.

relationships.name: authenticates
relationships.description: Or the person identity, for a human-held credential.

context.purpose: Points at a credential held by an issuing provider — which credential, held where, at what assurance — without the value ever entering the model.
context.plain_description: A reference to a secret, never the secret. It names the kind of credential (the required `credential_type`), the issuer that holds it (`issuer_ref`), the provider-side path it resolves at (`secret_path`), its `scope` — an object saying what it may operate on — and the minimum assurance the consumer requires (`required_assurance`). At realization the issuer resolves it and delivers the value directly to the authorized consumer — the value never passes through the model, audit, source control, or logs. What IS recorded: that it resolved, which version, and when it was first retrieved.
use_when: You need any resource (a container, a service, a BMC, a bind account) to consume a secret without the secret appearing in data.
You need audit facts about credential resolution and first retrieval, without exposure.
You need consumers to demand a minimum assurance level and have weaker issuers filtered out before binding.
not_for: The identity that authenticates with the credential — Identity.Person / Identity.ServiceAccount; an identity references its credentials, this is the credential side.
Storing an actual password, key, or token anywhere — no type is for that; the value lives only with the issuer.
works_with: Identity.Person / Identity.ServiceAccount — whose credential this is.
Compute.Container / Software.Service / Storage.FileShare — consumers that reference it from env, mounts, or config.
